correctness.rationale: For each canonical right-continuous BV input, the signed-derivative measure reduces the sharp quotient to single jumps. The negative-binomial tail equals the exact Beta(k,n+1) CDF, yielding integrated leakage E|B-s|. Convexity reduces to cell endpoints, a variance/tail bound makes the maximum finite, 326 exact Fraction comparisons certify degrees 1–7 and n=8 comparison, and explicit analytic opposing monotonicities prove all n>=8. Gamma-ratio CLT, L2 moment bounds, boundary tightness and a unique scalar maximum prove the sharp coefficient and one-third jump localization. Finite experiments are not used to prove the infinite statements; no attainment is claimed for n>=8.

The older integral MKZ papers modify the input sampling into an integral operator, so matching name does not transfer the exact claimed result.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Classical MKZ is also called a Bernstein power-series operator with negative-binomial weights. Reformulating the new quotient in terms of Beta CDF leakage or the adjoint step response leaves it distinct from pointwise absolute first moments: the latter fixes x and averages |sample-x|, whereas the new quotient fixes a jump location s and integrates the absolute discrepancy over x. Theorem 2.1 of Zeng–Cheng gives the same leading spatial shape but not the exact finite norm or transition.

value.rationale: This treats a natural exact norm for discontinuous-data approximation by a standard positive point-sampling scheme. The exact finite-degree supremum is algorithmically evaluable and a proved sharp degree-eight transition separates endpoint-only nonattainment from interior dominance; the large-degree coefficient and extremal jump retreat supply quantitative calibration. The transition is an all-degree motivated boundary, not an arbitrary fixed-n computation.
